direction_as_read: positive on a named primary outcome in two trials of about 110 women each, of the same extract the label prints; the abstracts do not state funding or independent replication
summary: One label (DSLD 232725, Menopause 731) prints ERr 731 Siberian Rhubarb (Rheum rhaponticum L.) extract 4 mg as its only active. PMID 16894335 (109 women) and PMID 19161045 (112 women) each report a significant fall in Menopause Rating Scale total score against placebo at 12 weeks, on a named primary outcome. Neither abstract prints the tablet's mg amount; PMID 42416823 prints 4 mg daily for a 112-woman randomized phase. Agent review gives no credit in this work; the question stays open for a human ruling. Abstracts only.
question_for_clinician: PMID 19161045 and PMID 16894335 test the label's exact extract on a named primary outcome in perimenopausal women. Do they justify credit to ERr 731 4 mg daily for menopausal symptoms, once the tablet's mg amount is confirmed from the full text, since the abstracts give it only as one tablet? Agent recommendation: this is a real candidate for your ruling, limited to ERr 731 and to perimenopausal symptoms; no credit is given by this review.

read_not_used.17213754: Stored trial. Same size and arms as PMID 16894335 (109 women, 54 and 55), reporting anxiety and well-being; the abstract names no primary outcome and prints one tablet, no mg. Positive for anxiety on the Hamilton scale.
read_not_used.18978638: Open observational extension, 48 plus 48 weeks, of the 109-woman trial; no concurrent control, though PubMed tags it Randomized Controlled Trial.
read_not_used.42973544: Narrative review; the abstract mentions rhapontic rhubarb among small randomized trials and gives no data for it.

stop_or_hold: The mg amount of the tablet in PMID 16894335 and PMID 19161045 is not in their abstracts, so their dose fields stay extraction_pending and 4 mg sits only on PMID 42416823.
